10.1002_adma.75302: Conversion‐type anode materials hold great promise for sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs), yet their practical rate performance is fundamentally constrained by sluggish reaction kinetics beyond mass‐transport limitations. Despite notable advances in accelerating ion/electron transport, intrinsically reducing the large reaction kinetic barrier and activation energy associated with robust metal–chalcogen (M─S) bonds remains a long‐standing challenge. In this study, we propose a universal spin‐polarization‐engineered (SPE) antibonding‐orbital modulation paradigm to fundamentally regulate M─S bond strength and enable ultrahigh‐rate sodium storage. As a proof of concept, magnetic manganese heteroatom doping into heterojunctions enhances the saturation magnetization by ∼210%, inducing a spin‐state transition from low‐spin to high‐spin configurations, which increases the electron occupation of antibonding orbitals formed between metal e g orbitals and chalcogen p orbitals, and thereby regulates M─S bond strength. Benefiting from this spin‐engineered electronic reconstruction, Mn‐FeS 2 /CoS 2 anode delivers an ultrahigh‐rate capability of 300 mA h g −1 at 120 A g −1 , together with exceptional long‐term durability (∼100% retention over 13 000 cycles at 100 A g −1 ), ranking among the best record. The generality of this strategy is further validated by extending SPE modulation to other magnetic dopants. Moreover, the industrial‐level pouch cell is assembled to demonstrate the practical potential of this strategy.
10.1002_aenm.71607: The practical application of perovskite solar cells (PerSCs) is still limited by their intrinsic instability, particularly under dynamic temperature fluctuations in outdoor conditions. In this study, we present a series of dual cross‐linking agents to improve the efficiency and temperature endurance of PerSCs. Specifically, 3‐(trichlorosilyl)propyl methacrylate (MPTCl) with multiple functional groups is applied to modify the upper interface of the perovskite. The ─C═O group exhibits strong interactions with the undercoordinated Pb 2+ on the perovskite surface, helping to stabilize structures and reduce interfacial charge recombination. The C═C bond of the methacrylate group undergoes in situ polymerization/cross‐linking, while the trichlorosilyl group undergoes hydrolysis and subsequent condensation under humid conditions, enabling MPTCl to form a Si─O─Si cross‐linked network. This cross‐linked interfacial layer improves interfacial structural stability and enhances resistance to moisture‐ and heat‐induced degradation. Consequently, the optimal PerSCs achieved a high power conversion efficiency of 26.22% and demonstrated enhanced thermal durability under simulated thermal cycling conditions, retaining 82.4% of their initial efficiency after 250 cycles. This work proposes a dual cross‐linking strategy that provides an effective route for simultaneously improving the efficiency and thermal resilience of PerSCs, offering valuable insights into the development of durable perovskite photovoltaic technologies.
10.1002_smll.202512808: Tin oxide (SnO 2 ) has been widely used as an electron transport layer (ETL) in perovskite solar cells (PSCs) due to the excellent charge transport properties. In this work, we present a comprehensive computational and experimental investigation of a low‐temperature strategy for developing Mg‐doped SnO 2 (Mg‐SnO 2 ) as an ETL to enhance the performance of indoor perovskite solar cells (i‐PSCs). Experimental results demonstrate that Mg incorporation enhances optical transparency, increases the bandgap, and improves charge transport by reducing charge recombination at the ETL/perovskite interface. These enhancements lead to superior PCEs, achieving 35.54% under indoor LED illumination and 20.28% under standard one sun conditions, significantly outperforming undoped SnO 2 ‐based devices. Complementary density functional theory (DFT) simulations support the experimental findings, revealing that Mg doping decreases deep trap states, and contribute to improved ETL conductivity. The strong correlation between theoretical predictions and experimental outcomes underscores the effectiveness of Mg‐SnO 2 as a high‐performance and stable ETL for indoor photovoltaic applications. This study establishes a practical pathway for developing optimized Mg‐doped electron transport layer for efficient indoor light harvesting.
10.1016_j.cej.2026.181962: Photoelectrochemical (PEC) ammonia synthesis from nitrate offers a sustainable approach to producing valuable chemicals while mitigating waste pollution. Here, we developed an ultrathin amorphous boron nitride (BN) passivation layer (∼5 nm) via magnetron sputtering, leveraging its strong adhesion and high uniformity on InP to enhance interfacial electron transportation to surface for ammonia generation. We found that nitrogen incorporation during BN deposition lead to more chemically uniform BN layer with enhanced nitridation and reduced oxidation, significantly reducing interfacial defects and suppressing surface-state-mediated recombination between cocatalyst (∼50 nm spin-coated TiOₓ) and InP semiconductor. The innovation is combining tunneling passivation layer BN with TiOₓ catalysis with Ti O active sites for improved charge-separation efficiency and photoelectrode stability, leading to high selectivity under near-bias-free conditions. The TiOₓ/BN/InP photocathode achieves near-unity FE at 0 V vs RHE, a pioneering demonstration of an InP photocathode for outperforming selective ammonia generation from nitrate electrolytes under solar illumination. This work demonstrates the feasibility of magnetron sputtering–fabricated ultrathin BN layers for enhancing selective PEC nitrate reduction, while providing insights into the effectiveness of interface engineering strategy in enabling selective ammonia production under mild operating conditions.
10.1016_j.est.2026.123955: The increasing price volatility in the Nordic electricity markets exposes households to a greater electricity bill risk. As the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) and rooftop photovoltaics (PV) grows, bidirectional charging (vehicle-to-home, V2H) enables households to arbitrage spot prices and shift their demand away from peaks. This study quantifies the economic value of combining PV with a mobile EV battery under Finnish spot-based pricing. We model three tariff cases: (i) fixed price; (ii) spot price without PV/EV; and (iii) spot price with PV+V2H and evaluate three investment configurations: PV + a bidirectional charger, adding a bidirectional charger, and upgrading from unidirectional to bidirectional charging. A 15-year net present value (NPV) analysis explicitly accounts for battery degradation. Under spot pricing, PV+V2H yields average annual electricity bill savings of €84 ( ≈ 4%). However, the estimated degradation costs ( €500/year) dominate, producing negative NPVs across all configurations: –€11,190 (full system deployment), –€5290 (charger addition), and –€4990 (charger upgrade). Sensitivity tests indicate that even with battery prices projected to fall to €69/kWh by 2028, PV+V2H systems remain uneconomic because degradation outweighs arbitrage savings. PV+V2H is thus not financially viable in Finland today due to limited further cost reductions, longer battery lifetimes, and the absence of supportive policy incentives.
10.1016_j.joule.2026.102539: Solid-state batteries promise high energy storage with enhanced safety but suffer from contact loss at the lithium (Li) metal anode-solid electrolyte interface as Li is stripped into the ionically-conducting solid electrolyte. Contrary to the prevailing view that the contact loss arises from void formation in the Li metal at this interface, we demonstrate, in cells with garnet electrolytes, that it instead arises from the deposition of insulating impurities from within the electrode onto the interface. These impurities form a porous layer, and an imposed stack pressure is required for Li to creep through the pores of this layer. This proposed mechanism is supported by our experimental observations that no voids are present on the interface and by our finding that contact loss persists at stack pressures that are sufficiently high to collapse any voids in the Li. Theoretical models developed using the impurity deposition mechanism are in excellent agreement with measurements. This finding has significant implications for improving the design of all solid-state batteries including the development of anode-free cells for which impurities within the electrode are expected to be substantially reduced.
10.1038_s41467-025-67982-0: Li-ion batteries, widely used in electronic devices, electric vehicles, and aviation, demand high energy density, fast charging capabilities, and broad operating temperature ranges. Computations combined with experiments have gained increasing attention for electrolyte development. However, the inherent complexity of electrolytes poses a significant challenge. Classical molecular dynamics often fails due to inaccuracies in force field parameters, while ab initio calculationsarelimitedbyhighcomputationalcosts. Recently, machinelearning molecular dynamics has emerged as an efficient and accurate alternative. However, its application is hindered by limited transferability of machine learning potentials. In this work, we developed a universal machine learning potential for electrolytes using an iterative training approach on randomly composed datasets, enabling the accurate computation of key properties for a broad range of electrolytes via molecular dynamics. Furthermore, coordination dynamics analysis of Li ion, by quantifying the coordination lifetime, provides a direct, quantitative measure of solvation strength. The universal machine learning potential for electrolytes facilitates the prediction and optimization of electrolyte properties, offering a powerful tool for electrolyte design.
